o1.biggest_strength: Ranks channels by retained users with the math, then builds the whole timeline and go/no-go gate around the migration risk the data exposes.
o1.biggest_mistake: The X post and email are a bit plain and the plan's tables are dense; nothing seriously wrong, just less craft in the customer-facing voice than the brand asks for.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Make the X thread and email feel more like Raycast (playful, one crisp demo) and trim the date table to the steps that matter.

o2.biggest_strength: Also ranks by retention, adds sharper gates (1,000 beta migrations, top-200 extension test, staged rollout thresholds) and gives a multi-post X thread with real craft and specific author credits.
o2.biggest_mistake: Still has bracketed placeholders ([first name], [Opens in __ ms], [author]) and a Product Hunt day that adds sequencing risk; a speed post tied to a made-up number is hinted at.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Fill or clean out the placeholders and lock the speed claim to a measured number so nothing in the drafts promises an unshipped figure.

reason: Both get the channel ranking and migration gate right, but Output 2's gates are sharper and its X thread feels more like Raycast; Output 2 just needs its placeholders cleaned before it can ship.
